messages:
maria: Heads-up — hit a weird mypy failure when calling the async Python client inside our retry decorator. Looks like the generated models lose Optional/Union hints when bundled with the auth wrapper. Anyone seen this?

kevin: Ugh, not surprising. Can you paste a tiny repro?

maria: Yep. Minimal:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
from retrying import retry

client = AsyncClient(api_key='x')

@retry
async def call():
    resp = await client.get_user(user_id=42)
    # mypy says 'User' has no attribute 'email' even though pydantic model shows Optional[str]
    return resp.email
```

maria: mypy output: `error: "User" has no attribute "email" (or "Item"?)` — but runtime is fine. Only fails in strict mode.

sam: Are you sure it's the retry decorator and not the autogen stubbing? Could be the decorator changing the signature from coroutine -> callable and mypy loses Awaitable annotation.

maria: Interesting — when I remove @retry, mypy is happy. So decorator wrapper is implicated. But why would that affect fields on the model type?

kevin: Two things could be happening: 1) the stub for AsyncClient.get_user is typed as `Any` in generated stubs when decorated at generation time, or 2) the decorator is a sync wrapper (returns Any) and mypy widens types through type inference. Do you have the generated sdk file version in your venv?

maria: It's from the wheel we ship: /usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages/redwood_sdk/async_client.py (autogenerated). The signature there is `async def get_user(self, user_id: int) -> User` — User defined in models.py. models.py has `email: Optional[str] = None` according to runtime `repr`.

sam: Could it be a forward-ref or stringified annotation issue? mypy sometimes can't resolve forward refs without proper `from __future__ import annotations` handling in stubs.

maria: I inspected the .pyi stub we generate in the sdist: the return annotation is `-> Any` for a bunch of endpoints. So generator is the culprit for stubs, but then why local install seems typed correctly?

kevin: Right — we generate both runtime models (pydantic) and .pyi stubs. The stub generation path is separate and sometimes strips Unions/Optionals into `Any` when it hits complex nested generics (we flattened for simplicity). That explains the mypy issue; the decorator only surfaces it because the retry wrapper signature interacts with how mypy narrows Awaitable -> return type.

maria: So the fix is to make generator preserve Optional/Union in stubs. Short-term, what's a clean workaround for users hitting this?

kevin: Add a typed retry wrapper that preserves the coroutine return type. Example: `from typing import TypeVar, Awaitable, Callable, ParamSpec` etc. Quick snippet: 
```py
from typing import TypeVar, Awaitable, Callable, ParamSpec
P = ParamSpec('P')
R = TypeVar('R')

def typed_retry(f: Callable[P, Awaitable[R]]) -> Callable[P, Awaitable[R]]:
    async def inner(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> R:
        return await retry_call(lambda: f(*args, **kwargs))
    return inner
```

kevin: That preserves the type for mypy. But obviously SDK side we should either produce accurate stubs or ship protocol-typed interfaces so decorators don't break inference.

maria: Thanks — that helps. I filed a quick ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-4321 (feel free to upvote).

sam: I'm adding a unit test to the generator repo to ensure Optional and Union are retained in .pyi outputs (and a mypy-based smoke test).

maria: One more twist — when using `client.get_user(..., include_fields=['email'])` (a param that toggles optional fields), the generated typed response becomes `User | None` in runtime but the stub generator currently emits `Any` for conditional shapes. That makes it impossible to statically assert `resp.email`.

kevin: That's a design decision we made to avoid combinatorial types, but we should at least preserve the more specific types in stubs for common cases. I'll scope a patch: preserve `Optional[...]` and simple `Union[A, None]` and avoid collapsing to Any for those. For complex discriminated unions we can keep Any with comments.

maria: For onboarding docs: can we add a small note on the README about the typed-retry wrapper pattern and a recommended mypy config to relax only this area? Many users will hit this when they apply decorators (auth, retry, metrics).

kevin: Agreed. I'll add a short section in SDK docs and a code sample. Also will surface `py.typed` in the wheel so tools know it's typed.

sam: ci-bot: created branch `fix/pyi-preserve-optionals` and added a draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/pull/987

ci-bot: build passed for branch fix/pyi-preserve-optionals (unit tests + flake) :white_check_mark:

maria: Awesome. Until the release lands, workaround above + `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` or `cast(User, resp).email` if folks are stuck. But prefer typed wrapper.

kevin: Thanks for reporting — this is subtle and worth documenting. Follow-up: I'll add a lint check to generator to avoid accidental `Any` in exported stubs for model returns.

maria: Thanks all. I'll update the issue with the repro and a link to this thread. :heart:

kevin: Ping me if you want me to pair on the pyi generator changes later today.
